findings.reason: Lock object adapter->ptp_lock (spin_lock_init at drivers/net/ethernet/chelsio/cxgb4/cxgb4_ptp.c:432) is shared between a TIMER_SOFTIRQ callback and BH-enabled process-context transmit code with NO bottom-half disable at either the timer side or the xmit holder side - the timer-softirq analogue of the seed's missing spin_lock_bh invariant, and the same lock-object shape already confirmed in sibling snapshot s01 (fact f024). UNTRUSTED SOURCE (attacker-influenced concurrency, not data): any PTP event frame transmitted through the Chelsio interface (is_ptp_enabled(skb, dev) branch at sge.c:2473) aligns the process-context holder, and pending tx-timer expiry (s->tx_timer is re-armed whenever TX descriptors are outstanding) aligns the timer side on the same CPU; ordinary traffic plus timer expiry is enough. TIMER-SOFTIRQ SIDE: timer_setup(&s->tx_timer, sge_tx_timer_cb, 0) at sge.c:5200 registers sge_tx_timer_cb (body at sge.c:4270) which takes adap->ptp_lock with plain spin_lock at sge.c:4290 (unlock 4297) while reclaiming ptptxq TX descriptors, and executes in call_timer_fn from TIMER_SOFTIRQ with no BH disable. PROCESS SIDE (holder): t4_start_xmit (netdev .ndo_start_xmit, sge.c:2462) takes spin_lock(&adap->ptp_lock) plainly at sge.c:2477 around cxgb4_eth_xmit(skb, dev) in the PTP-enabled branch; ndo_start_xmit runs in BH-enabled process context (direct xmit from __dev_queue_xmit only disables preemption via local_bh_disable around the qdisc lock, and the PTP branch is also reached from qdisc dequeue under NET_TX softirq where BH is enabled after the qdisc root_lock is dropped); the loopback PTP path also takes the same lock plainly at cxgb4_ptp.c:115 (cxgb4_ptp_read_hwstamp, called from t4_tx_hststamp sge.c:3549->3555 invoked at sge.c:3738 inside cxgb4_eth_xmit while the 2477 plain hold is on the stack). MISSING GUARANTEE: no spin_lock_bh/local_bh_disable at 2477, 4290 or cxgb4_ptp.c:115; the only _bh site on this lock in the snapshot is the teardown at sge.c:4966 (spin_lock_bh(&adap->ptp_lock) in t4_free_sge ptptxq cleanup), proving the driver knows the lock requires BH disable at process-context sites. CONSEQUENCE: a TIMER_SOFTIRQ firing on the same CPU while the plain xmit-side holder is between 2477 and 2479 spins forever on ptp_lock while the preempted holder can never resume - softirq/soft-lockup, RCU stall, device TX stall, repeatable DoS; the exact timer-softirq analogue of the ks7010 tx_dev_lock seed mechanism. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: no spin_lock_bh/irqsave variant exists at any non-teardown ptp_lock site (only 2477, 4290, cxgb4_ptp.c:115, 4966); the window requires PTP hardware timestamping enabled (is_ptp_enabled) and a tx-timer expiry coinciding with a PTP frame transmission on the same CPU; no runtime reproducer was possible (snapshot lacks .config/generated headers).

limitations: Search bounded to snapshot s09 only, as required by the intent; no other snapshot was inspected.

Bounded by the finalize directive: the systematic whole-tree enumeration of timer_list/hrtimer/delayed_work callback bodies containing plain spin_lock (the ~60-70 callback family enumerated in sibling passes) was not re-run for s09; deep lock-object pairing was completed only for the highest-priority timer-branch shapes: br_multicast br->multicast_lock, libiscsi session->frwd_lock, cxgb4 adap->ptp_lock, tun tun->lock, garp.c/mrp.c app->lock.

Unresolved candidates left for follow-up in s09: iwlwifi pcie/tx.c txq->lock stuck-timer, qdisc root_lock in sch_pie/sch_sfq/sch_red perturbation timers, bcm63xx_enet refill-rx timer, hostap ap_handle_timer sta_table_lock, and the remaining timer callbacks enumerated in sibling passes (xfrm, ipvs, neighbour, taprio, watchdogs, eql, sunrpc xprt transport_lock) that were not re-verified here.

hrtimer handlers and delayed_work timer-expiry callbacks were not separately enumerated in s09; delayed_work user callbacks run in worker (process) context so only direct timer_list callbacks were treated as the timer-softirq side.

The cxgb4 finding is a static hypothesis: no runtime reproducer, lockdep run, or compile was performed (the s09 tree lacks .config and generated headers for standalone builds); the deadlock window additionally requires PTP hardware timestamping enabled on a Chelsio T5+ interface (is_ptp_enabled(skb, dev), sge.c:2473) and a tx-timer expiry coinciding with a PTP frame transmission on the same CPU, which is reflected in medium confidence.

Whether the t4_start_xmit PTP branch at 2477 can also run under NET_TX softirq with a BH state that makes the plain lock safe was not separately proven; the process-context direct-xmit entry (the dangerous direction) plus the timer softirq side is the reported basis.
The literal ks7010 seed is absent from s09 (no drivers/staging/ks7010 directory); per instructions the seed must never be reported regardless.
